records.text: CERN's Large Hadron Collider is a 17-mile tunnel near Geneva, reaches roughly 600 feet underground in places, and collides subatomic particles at high speed.
records.speaker: Mark (Candace show producer; surname unverified)

appearances.snippet: and peter higgs i believe and so the search was on to find this particle and so that's why cern created the large hadron collider which is based in geneva switzerland and is a 17 mile tunnel underground up to 600 feet underground in some places where they shoot particles at subatomic particles at each other at a very high speed to try and break them apart to see what they're found what they're composed of

verification.notes: CERN describes the LHC as a 27-kilometre ring near Geneva where high-energy beams travel near light speed and collide. Its official guide gives tunnel depths of 50 to 175 metres, making the maximum about 574 feet and the statement's rough 600-foot figure reasonable.

sources.title: The Large Hadron Collider — CERN
sources.relevance: Official CERN page confirms the 27-km ring, Geneva-area location, high-speed beams, and collisions.

sources.title: LHC the guide — CERN
sources.relevance: Official CERN guide gives the tunnel depth range as 50 to 175 metres, approximately 574 feet at maximum.
